run.description: Import a pack into the yard: set the yard to what the pack says
does: pack telegram (embedded in yardr unknown), of kind source, into the yard: it adds 1 source and copies 2 command files (6 commands), and changes nothing else. It grants no call, makes no hook, and sets no credential's file.

source telegram: its calls go to https://api.telegram.org. Its credential is the variable TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (the name, never the value), sent in the request path wherever the declaration puts {credential} (credential.in_path: true): it stands in the logs of every server on the way. It has no second credential for updates, no mint, no header of its own.

call message (update): POST /bot{credential}/sendMessage. It takes chat (string, required, pattern ^-?[0-9]+$), title (string, required, at most 250) and text (string, required, at most 3800), and sends no query.
call message sends the body {"chat_id":"{chat}","text":"{title}\n{text}"}. Its answer is returned as it comes, at most 65536 bytes.

call document (update): POST /bot{credential}/sendDocument. It takes chat (string, required, pattern ^-?[0-9]+$), path (file, required, at most 52428800) and caption (string, optional, at most 1024), and sends no query.
call document sends the body {"caption":"{caption}","chat_id":"{chat}","document":"{path}"}. Its answer is returned as it comes, at most 65536 bytes.
call setwebhook (update): POST /bot{credential}/setWebhook. It takes url (string, required, at most 2048) and secret_token (string, required, at most 256), and sends no query.
call setwebhook sends the body {"allowed_updates":["message"],"secret_token":"{secret_token}","url":"{url}"}. Its answer is returned as it comes, at most 65536 bytes.
call webhookinfo (read): GET /bot{credential}/getWebhookInfo. It takes no parameter, and sends no query.
call webhookinfo sends no body. Its answer is returned as it comes, at most 65536 bytes.
Its check call is webhookinfo; it names no idempotency header.

it can tell a user: the call message, whose chat takes the person's address, read as TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID from the person's own env file; the title fills title and the text fills text and it takes no link.
it hears deliveries: only one whose chat is the address of a user told through it, read as TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID, and only an operator's: another's, and a stranger's, is dropped after verification.
it speaks in threads: it names no place to open one; it names no state words; it takes no labels; it assigns nobody.

what it sends in: deliveries are verified by the header X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token holding the hook's secret itself (scheme secret); a delivery is named by update_id in its body; it sends no timestamp; bodies are unique; the command [telegram/normalize] turns a verified body into the envelope, handed no credential; its events may carry the fields chat; the yard registers its webhook with setwebhook (POST /bot{credential}/setWebhook), filling url with the public URL and secret_token with the hook's secret.
it has no limits command, no bead link, no identity fold (its identity keys keep their case) and no pull-request or CI events.

command file telegram/thread: [telegram/thread, reply] (thread.reply, handed the credential), [telegram/thread, posted] (thread.posted, handed the credential), [telegram/thread, read] (thread.read, handed the credential), [telegram/thread, get] (thread.file, handed the credential) and [telegram/thread, tell] (notify.image, handed the credential): sha256 944e82d156f6250160c75aa7a8508034e0f51405913e62253ce2b9d7759ee81d, mode 0700
command file telegram/normalize: [telegram/normalize] (hook.normalize, handed no credential): sha256 c714468df423c9cfe851dc5d51776e273e7e74ae9021b21131a05a85da6a8e35, mode 0700
still owed after it: the credential, by a secret ask for telegram; and which user it tells, by yardr user set <user> notify=telegram.

carried.name: telegram
carried.text:
# Telegram as a declared source: one message or one file to one chat
# through the Bot API's sendMessage and sendDocument, each a POST with
# the bot's token in the path and the chat's id in the body: a message
# goes as JSON, a file as an upload. The notify key makes it a source a
# user can be told through (yardr user set <name> notify=telegram); the
# hook key hears operator-role users' chats back, answered with yardr reply.
# The check call reads what Telegram holds of the webhook
# (getWebhookInfo): its url, its pending_update_count, and the last
# failed delivery's date and message, which say a broken webhook from a
# quiet person, whose chat has no steady rhythm to time silence by.
#
# Checked against core.telegram.org/bots/api on 24 October 2026: queries
# are https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD_NAME; sendMessage takes
# chat_id (Integer or String, required) and text (1-4096 characters,
# required); sendDocument takes chat_id and the file as a multipart
# upload (50 MB at most), with an optional caption (1024 characters at
# most); each answers 200 with the message on success. Receiving is a
# webhook carrying one Update, authenticated with the secret token in the
# X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header, compared as it arrives; each
# Update carries its own update_id, by which a retry is told.
#
# The service has one text where the yard has a title and a text, so the
# body carries both: the title first (who and what: "mail from mckean"),
# then the text. Their bounds leave the body under the service's 4096.
# The chat id goes as a string of digits: the notify key fills text, and
# the service takes either form. A person's chat is its numeric id, which
# the file holds every address to; the @username form names a channel.
name: telegram
about: Messages with a person's phone through Telegram.
base: https://api.telegram.org
credential:
  env: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN            # the bot's token: the name, never the value
  in_path: true                      # the service takes it in the path (/bot<token>/...)
calls:
  message:
    kind: update
    about: One message to one chat
    params:
      chat:  { type: string, pattern: "^-?[0-9]+$" }
      title: { type: string, max: 250 }
      text:  { type: string, max: 3800 }
    request:
      method: POST
      path: /bot{credential}/sendMessage
      body: { chat_id: "{chat}", text: "{title}\n{text}" }
  document:
    kind: update
    about: One file to one chat
    params:
      chat:    { type: string, pattern: "^-?[0-9]+$" }
      path:    { type: file, max: 52428800 }
      caption: { type: string, max: 1024, optional: true }
    request:
      method: POST
      path: /bot{credential}/sendDocument
      body: { chat_id: "{chat}", document: "{path}", caption: "{caption}" }
  setwebhook:
    kind: update
    about: Tell Telegram where to send updates (setWebhook)
    params:
      url:          { type: string, max: 2048 }
      secret_token: { type: string, max: 256 }
    request:
      method: POST
      path: /bot{credential}/setWebhook
      body: { url: "{url}", secret_token: "{secret_token}", allowed_updates: ["message"] }
  webhookinfo:
    kind: read
    about: What Telegram holds of the webhook (getWebhookInfo)
    request:
      method: GET
      path: /bot{credential}/getWebhookInfo
check: webhookinfo
notify:
  call: message
  address: { param: chat, env: TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID }   # the person's own chat id, read from the user's env_file
  title: title                                      # yardr's value -> the call's parameter
  text: text
  image: [telegram/thread, tell]                    # with a picture, the command sends it with the caption instead

# ---- what it sends us ----------------------------------------------------

hook:
  # Adapter.Verify stays data, checked by the core: the webhook secret is
  # handed to no command, and an unverified body reaches none. Telegram
  # sends no signature over the body, only the secret itself in the header.
  verify:
    scheme: secret
    signature: { header: X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token }
    delivery: { body: update_id }   # the Update's own id: a retry repeats it, re-serialized or not
  bodies: unique

  # The yard registers the webhook itself on the hook card: it makes
  # the secret, and calls setWebhook with the public URL and it.
  register:
    call: setwebhook
    url: url
    secret: secret_token

  # Adapter.Normalize. stdin {"headers":{…},"body":{…}}, stdout the
  # envelope. The core sets source and delivery itself.
  normalize: [telegram/normalize]

  # The keys its events' fields may carry: a subscription's --where may
  # name them beside type, action, team, project, repo and label.
  keys: [chat]

# ---- what the yard does in its threads ------------------------------------
# One command per thing, each handed its object on stdin and the
# credential under TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, with YARDR_SOURCE_BASE from base
# above. The service gives a bot no history to read and no idempotency
# key to set, so posted and read answer what there is to find: nothing.
# file fetches what a kept delivery's photo, document, voice, video or
# audio names (getFile, then the file), with the source's own token, into
# the blob store: at most the yard's blob_max_bytes and the script's
# TELEGRAM_MAX_BYTES (8 MiB), whichever is lower; the Bot API serves a bot
# files up to 20 MB. files says replies take files: with them, the reply
# sends pictures by sendPhoto and anything else by sendDocument, the text
# as the caption where it fits in 1024 characters. The shapes are in
# docs/integrations.md.

thread:
  reply:  [telegram/thread, reply]      # in  {thread, parent, body, key}      out {id}
  posted: [telegram/thread, posted]     # in  {thread, key}                    out {} always
  read:   [telegram/thread, read]       # in  {thread}                         out {messages: []} always
  file:   [telegram/thread, get]        # in  {ref, dir, max_bytes}            out {path, bytes}
  files: true                           # replies take files: reply's in gains files: [paths]

# ---- which chats are heard ------------------------------------------------
# Not the mirror of notify: a delivery is kept only when its chat is the
# address of a user whose env file sets the address, read from the file
# as telling reads it. Anyone can find the bot's name and write to it,
# so any other chat is dropped: answered 200, recorded nowhere.

hear:
  field: chat
  address: { env: TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID }
  from: operator                        # operator-role users' chats; a member's is dropped like a stranger's
  # A claim approved subscribes the yard's hearer to this chat with
  # type=message beside it: the chat's other Updates (edits, member
  # changes) are noise nobody asked to hear.
  subscribe: { type: message }

files.text:
#!/bin/bash
# thread: what the yard does in a Telegram chat: reply, posted, read, get,
# and tell for notify.image. One JSON object on stdin, one on stdout, as
# the thread key of the declaration says, and the notify key for tell.
# TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and YARDR_SOURCE_BASE, the declaration's base,
# are in the environment. Needs curl, jq, file and the standard shell
# utilities it calls (grep, head, wc, tr).
#
# The service gives a bot no history to read and no idempotency key to
# set, so posted and read answer what there is to find, nothing, and a
# reply retried after a lost answer posts twice.
set -euo pipefail
in=$(cat)
arg() { jq -r --arg k "$1" '.[$k] // ""' <<<"$in"; }

send_message() { # one text to the chat, by sendMessage; prints the message's id
  text=$1
  # The token is part of the address, and an argument can be read by every
  # process on the machine while curl runs: the address goes to curl as a
  # config line on its stdin, written by the shell itself.
  out=$(printf 'url = "%s"\n' "$YARDR_SOURCE_BASE/bot$TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN/sendMessage" \
    | curl -sS --fail-with-body -K - \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "$(jq -n -c --arg c "$thread" --arg t "$text" '{chat_id: $c, text: $t}')") || {
    code=$?
    desc=$(describe "$out")
    echo "sendMessage to chat $thread failed${desc:+: $desc} (curl exit $code)" >&2
    return 1
  }
  jq -e .ok >/dev/null <<<"$out" 2>/dev/null || {
    desc=$(describe "$out")
    echo "${desc:-sendMessage failed}" >&2
    return 1
  }
  mid=$(jq -r '(.result.message_id // "") | tostring' <<<"$out" 2>/dev/null) && [ -n "$mid" ] || {
    echo "sendMessage answered no message" >&2
    return 1
  }
  printf '%s' "$mid"
}

describe() { # what the service said of a refusal, for an error the daemon logs: one line of printable characters, 200 at most, the token and chat id taken out should the service echo them. The delete names its range in octal because busybox tr reads [:print:] with -c as literal characters.
  local d
  d=$(jq -r '.description // empty' <<<"$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\000-\037\177') || d=""
  d=${d//"$TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN"/}
  d=${d//"$thread"/}
  printf '%s' "${d:0:200}"
}

qform() { # a value for curl's -F, quoted, so that a ; or , or " in a file's name is no part of the option's syntax
  local s=${1//\\/\\\\}
  printf '"%s"' "${s//\"/\\\"}"
}

send_media() { # one picture or document to the chat, by sendPhoto or sendDocument; prints the message's id
  method=$1; field=$2; file=$3; caption=$4
  [ -f "$file" ] || { echo "$method found no file at $file" >&2; return 1; }
  # The part goes with a type and a name, as a client's upload does. A
  # file the yard keeps is called by its hash, which names nothing a
  # person could open: it goes as photo.png or document.
  mime=$(file -b --mime-type "$file" 2>/dev/null) || mime=""
  [[ $mime =~ ^[a-z0-9.+_-]+/[a-z0-9.+_-]+$ ]] || mime=application/octet-stream
  name=${file##*/}
  if [[ $name =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]]; then
    case "$mime" in
    image/png) name=$field.png ;;
    image/jpeg) name=$field.jpg ;;
    image/gif) name=$field.gif ;;
    image/webp) name=$field.webp ;;
    image/bmp) name=$field.bmp ;;
    *) name=$field ;;
    esac
  fi
  # The address goes to curl on its stdin, as send_message's does; the
  # chat and the caption go as data, never parsed for @ or <. An error
  # names the method and what the service said, not the chat: a tell's
  # error is logged and recorded, and the chat is the person's address.
  args=(--form-string "chat_id=$thread" -F "$field=@$(qform "$file");type=$mime;filename=$(qform "$name")")
  if [ -n "$caption" ]; then args+=(--form-string "caption=$caption"); fi
  out=$(printf 'url = "%s"\n' "$YARDR_SOURCE_BASE/bot$TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN/$method" \
    | curl -sS --fail-with-body -K - "${args[@]}") || {
    code=$?
    desc=$(describe "$out")
    echo "$method failed${desc:+: $desc} (curl exit $code)" >&2
    return 1
  }
  jq -e .ok >/dev/null <<<"$out" 2>/dev/null || {
    desc=$(describe "$out")
    echo "$method failed${desc:+: $desc}" >&2
    return 1
  }
  mid=$(jq -r '(.result.message_id // "") | tostring' <<<"$out" 2>/dev/null) && [ -n "$mid" ] || {
    echo "$method answered no message" >&2
    return 1
  }
  printf '%s' "$mid"
}

case "$1" in
reply) # sendMessage to the chat the delivery came from; with files, the
  # text is the caption of the first picture or document instead. The
  # parent is left out: a chat is one conversation, and the key is left
  # out with it: the service takes no idempotency key.
  thread=$(arg thread)
  body=$(arg body)
  [ -n "$thread" ] || { echo "thread.reply was handed no thread" >&2; exit 1; }
  [ -n "$body" ] || { echo "thread.reply was handed no body" >&2; exit 1; }
  : "${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN:?TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN is not set}"
  : "${YARDR_SOURCE_BASE:?YARDR_SOURCE_BASE is not set}"
  nfiles=$(jq '.files | length' <<<"$in")
  if ! [ "$nfiles" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    id=$(send_message "$body")
    jq -n -c --arg id "$id" '{id: $id}'
    exit 0
  fi
  # A caption holds 1024 characters: a longer text goes first as its own
  # message, and the files follow without one, so no words are lost and
  # the order is kept. Several files go one after another, no album.
  caption="$body"
  id=""
  if [ "$(jq -n --arg b "$body" '$b | length')" -gt 1024 ]; then
    id=$(send_message "$body")
    caption=""
  fi
  i=0
  first=1
  while [ "$i" -lt "$nfiles" ]; do
    file=$(jq -r ".files[$i]" <<<"$in")
    [ -n "$file" ] || { echo "thread.reply was handed no file" >&2; exit 1; }
    [ -f "$file" ] || { echo "thread.reply found no file at $file" >&2; exit 1; }
    mime=$(file -b --mime-type "$file" 2>/dev/null) || { echo "thread.reply cannot read $file" >&2; exit 1; }
    # Only the kinds the service shows as a photo go by sendPhoto; a vector
    # drawing or a camera's raw file, which it cannot, goes as a document,
    # which takes any file.
    case "$mime" in
    image/png | image/jpeg | image/gif | image/webp | image/bmp) method=sendPhoto; field=photo ;;
    *) method=sendDocument; field=document ;;
    esac
    cap=""
    if [ "$first" -eq 1 ]; then cap="$caption"; first=0; fi
    mid=$(send_media "$method" "$field" "$file" "$cap")
    [ -n "$id" ] || id="$mid"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  [ -n "$id" ] || { echo "thread.reply posted nothing" >&2; exit 1; }
  jq -n -c --arg id "$id" '{id: $id}' ;;
tell) # one picture with its caption to the chat, for notify.image: in
  # {address, title, text, image}, out {status}. The caption is the title
  # then the text, cut to the service's 1024 characters.
  thread=$(arg address)
  title=$(arg title)
  text=$(arg text)
  image=$(arg image)
  [ -n "$thread" ] || { echo "notify.image was handed no address" >&2; exit 1; }
  [ -n "$image" ] || { echo "notify.image was handed no image" >&2; exit 1; }
  : "${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN:?TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN is not set}"
  : "${YARDR_SOURCE_BASE:?YARDR_SOURCE_BASE is not set}"
  caption=$(jq -nr --arg t "$title" --arg x "$text" '[$t, $x] | map(select(. != "")) | join("\n") | .[0:1024]')
  send_media sendPhoto photo "$image" "$caption" >/dev/null
  printf '%s' '{"status":200}' ;;
get) # The file a kept delivery names, by getFile and then the file's own
  # address, into the directory the core made: in {ref, dir, max_bytes},
  # out {path, bytes}. TELEGRAM_MAX_BYTES bounds a file as the yard's own
  # cap (max_bytes) does, and the lower holds; one over it is refused
  # before or while it downloads, with nothing left behind.
  TELEGRAM_MAX_BYTES=8388608
  id=$(jq -r '.ref.id // ""' <<<"$in")
  dir=$(arg dir)
  max=$(jq -r '.max_bytes // 0 | floor' <<<"$in")
  [ -n "$id" ] || { echo "thread.get was handed no ref.id" >&2; exit 1; }
  [ -d "$dir" ] || { echo "thread.get was handed no directory" >&2; exit 1; }
  : "${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN:?TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN is not set}"
  : "${YARDR_SOURCE_BASE:?YARDR_SOURCE_BASE is not set}"
  limit=$TELEGRAM_MAX_BYTES
  if [ "$max" -gt 0 ] && [ "$max" -lt "$limit" ]; then limit=$max; fi
  # The token is in both addresses: each goes to curl on its stdin, as
  # reply's does.
  out=$(printf 'url = "%s"\n' "$YARDR_SOURCE_BASE/bot$TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN/getFile" \
    | curl -sS --fail-with-body -K - \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "$(jq -n -c --arg f "$id" '{file_id: $f}')" 2>/dev/null) || {
    code=$?
    echo "getFile failed (curl exit $code)" >&2
    exit 1
  }
  jq -e .ok >/dev/null <<<"$out" 2>/dev/null || {
    # The response is outside the yard and can echo the token in the URL;
    # it is kept as a delivery's failure reason, so only say what failed.
    echo "getFile failed" >&2
    exit 1
  }
  jq -e '(.result.file_path | type) == "string"' >/dev/null <<<"$out" 2>/dev/null || {
    echo "getFile answered no file path" >&2
    exit 1
  }
  jq -e '(.result.file_size == null) or ((.result.file_size | type) == "number" and .result.file_size >= 0)' \
    >/dev/null <<<"$out" 2>/dev/null || {
    echo "getFile answered no file size" >&2
    exit 1
  }
  path=$(jq -r '.result.file_path' <<<"$out" 2>/dev/null) || {
    echo "getFile answered no file path" >&2
    exit 1
  }
  size=$(jq -r '.result.file_size // 0 | floor' <<<"$out" 2>/dev/null) || {
    echo "getFile answered no file size" >&2
    exit 1
  }
  # The path goes into an address on a config line: a path of the
  # service's own shape, never one that climbs or closes the quote.
  case "$path" in
  "" | *..* | /*) echo "getFile answered no file path" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  if ! grep -Eq '^[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+$' <<<"$path"; then
    echo "getFile answered no file path" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ "$size" -gt "$limit" ]; then
    echo "$size bytes, over the limit of $limit" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  # The response is arbitrary file content, so keep the temporary copy
  # owner-only even if the server was started with a permissive umask.
  umask 077
  file="$dir/file"
  printf 'url = "%s"\n' "$YARDR_SOURCE_BASE/file/bot$TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN/$path" \
    | curl -sS --fail -K - --max-filesize "$limit" 2>/dev/null \
    | head -c "$((limit + 1))" >"$file" || {
    code=$?
    n=$(wc -c <"$file" | tr -d ' ')
    rm -f "$file"
    if [ "$code" -eq 63 ] || [ "$n" -gt "$limit" ]; then
      echo "over the limit of $limit bytes" >&2
    else
      echo "the file did not download (curl exit $code)" >&2
    fi
    exit 1
  }
  n=$(wc -c <"$file" | tr -d ' ')
  if [ "$n" -gt "$limit" ]; then
    rm -f "$file"
    echo "$n bytes, over the limit of $limit" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  jq -n -c --arg p "$file" --argjson n "$n" '{path: $p, bytes: $n}' ;;
posted) # {} always: without an idempotency key there is nothing to find
  printf '%s' '{}' ;;
read) # no history: a bot cannot read a chat
  printf '%s' '{"messages":[]}' ;;
*) echo "unknown: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

#!/bin/sh
# A verified Telegram Update to the yard's envelope: stdin
# {"headers":{…},"body":{…}}, stdout the envelope. Needs jq.
# internal/hooks feeds it the Update bodies its tests recorded and compares
# the envelopes with the design's (sections 3.3 and 3.7 of
# docs/design/2026-10-13-yardr-c55e-telegram-hears.md).
#
# Every Update gets an envelope, a stranger's and an unknown kind too: the
# hear key drops chats not belonging to operator-role users after this
# returns, and a
# non-zero exit would be answered 400, which the service retries. Nothing
# of the body is ever printed to stderr.
exec jq -c '
def obj: if type == "object" then . else {} end;
def str($v): if ($v | type) == "string" then $v elif $v == null then "" else "\($v)" end;
# trunc is hooks.truncate: whitespace collapsed, at most 500 runes. The jq
# POSIX space class includes the Unicode spaces split by Go strings.Fields.
def trunc: (gsub("^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$"; "") | gsub("[[:space:]]+"; " ")) | if length > 500 then .[0:499] + "…" else . end;
def ordered: reduce .[] as $x ([]; if index($x) then . else . + [$x] end);
# mentions is the envelope'"'"'s standard shape: the lowercase names a text
# mentions with @, once each, in order. An @name in code is text, not a
# mention. A Telegram username is at most 32 letters, digits and _.
def mentions($md):
  ((($md // "") | gsub("(?s)```.*?(```|$)|`[^`\n]*`"; " "))
   | [scan("(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9_@./-])@([A-Za-z0-9_]+)")
      | .[0] | ascii_downcase | select(length <= 32)]
   | ordered);
# display is how the service names a user or a private chat: first and
# last name, else the username.
def display($u):
  ($u | obj) as $o
  | ([($o.first_name // ""), ($o.last_name // "")] | map(select(type == "string" and . != "")) | join(" ")) as $n
  | if $n != "" then $n else (($o.username // "") | if type == "string" then . else "" end) end;
# mmss is a duration in seconds as the phone shows it.
def mmss: (. / 60 | floor) as $m | (. % 60) as $s | "\($m):\(if $s < 10 then "0" else "" end)\($s)";
def nonblank: if type == "string" and . != "" then . else null end;
# fileref is a file the message carries as the envelope names it: the
# service'"'"'s file_id, the name the sender gave, the kind, the size where
# the service said. Fetched by thread get once the delivery is kept; this
# is handed no credential and fetches nothing.
def fileref($kind):
  obj
  | select((.file_id | type) == "string" and .file_id != "")
  | {id: .file_id, type: $kind}
    + (if (.file_name | type) == "string" and .file_name != "" then {name: .file_name} else {} end)
    + (if (.file_size | type) == "number" then {size: .file_size} else {} end);
# files are the message'"'"'s photo (its largest size, by file_size, else the
# last the service lists), document, voice, video and audio. A sticker,
# an animation and a video note stay their bracketed note alone.
def files($m):
  [ ($m.photo | if type == "array" and length > 0
                then (if any(.[]; (obj | .file_size | type) == "number")
                      then max_by(obj | .file_size // 0) else last end)
                     | fileref("photo")
                else empty end),
    ($m.document // empty | fileref("document")),
    ($m.voice // empty | fileref("voice")),
    ($m.video // empty | fileref("video")),
    ($m.audio // empty | fileref("audio")) ];

(.body | if type == "object" then . else error("telegram Update is not an object") end) as $u
| (($u.message | obj) | if ((.chat | obj).id) == null then null else . end) as $m
| if $m != null then
    ($m.chat | obj) as $chat
    | (($chat.id) | "\(.)") as $id
    | (($m.text | nonblank) // ($m.caption | nonblank)
       // (if ($m.photo // null) != null then "[photo]"
           elif ($m.document // null) != null then
             ((($m.document | obj).file_name // "") | if type == "string" and . != "" then "[document: \(.)]" else "[document]" end)
           elif ($m.voice // null) != null then
             ((($m.voice | obj).duration // null) | if type == "number" then "[voice message \(.|mmss)]" else "[voice message]" end)
           elif ($m.video // null) != null then "[video]"
           elif ($m.video_note // null) != null then "[video note]"
           elif ($m.audio // null) != null then "[audio]"
           elif ($m.animation // null) != null then "[animation]"
           elif ($m.sticker // null) != null then "[sticker]"
           else "[message]" end)) as $text
    | {source: "telegram", type: "message", action: "create",
       actor: {id: str(($m.from | obj).id), name: display($m.from)},
       thread: {id: $id, title: (if ($chat.type // "") == "private"
                                 then display($chat) else str($chat.title) end)},
       text: ($text | trunc), mentions: mentions($text),
       message: str($m.message_id), parent: str(($m.reply_to_message | obj).message_id),
       fields: {chat: [$id]}}
    + (files($m) | if length > 0 then {files: .} else {} end)
  else
    ([$u.edited_message, $u.channel_post, $u.edited_channel_post,
      $u.my_chat_member, $u.chat_member, $u.chat_join_request,
      $u.message_reaction, $u.message_reaction_count]
     | map(((. | obj | .chat | obj).id) | select(. != null)) | .[0]) as $cid
    | ([$u.callback_query]
       | map((((. | obj | .message | obj).chat | obj).id) | select(. != null)) | .[0]) as $qcid
    | ($cid // $qcid) as $found
    | {source: "telegram", type: "update", actor: {}, thread: {}, mentions: []}
    | if $found == null then . else . + {fields: {chat: ["\($found)"]}} end
  end
'
